verdict.rationale: Raygun documents automatic capture of diagnostics for every error occurrence. It has a JavaScript crash-reporting language guide with source-map decoding and .NET SDK features such as SendInBackground. Community users confirm open-source .NET and WinRT providers, and dSYM/ProGuard uploads point to iOS/Android mobile crash reporting. However, the pack never names or documents the official web, backend and mobile SDKs together, nor confirms that uncaught exceptions are hooked automatically. Missing for 10: an explicit list of official SDKs across web/backend/mobile, docs for automatic uncaught-exception handlers per platform, named mobile SDK documentation, independent hands-on corroboration of current platform coverage.

support.subject: As a developer, I can instrument my web frontend, backend services, and mobile apps with official SDKs that capture uncaught errors automatically

citations.quote: Raygun automatically captures detailed diagnostics for each and every error occurrence including full stack traces, method/function and class name data, OS, device, browser, location, host
Raygun uses them to take un-readable errors generated from minified JavaScript and translate them to be readable and to include code snippets from your source.
You'll need your external access token for the following services: Deployments API, Sending dSYMS to Raygun, Uploading ProGuard mapping files
Enhanced SendInBackground to queue messages for sending: Prevents SNAT exhaustion in .NET Core Azure environments.
